problems.description: Deleted the seed baseline (index.ts, the Express Todo API) entirely rather than building on it — the commit replaces the task domain with a different application, evidenced by package-lock.json declaring name "ssg" with gray-matter/marked (a static-site generator), which contradicts the Todo API seed.

The greenfield rewrite diverges from the baseline's established structure (models/routes/error-handling seams), throwing away the seams the seed was designed to provide for multi-session story continuity.
61 convention violations measured (convention score 0.59): functions use snake_case, classes and interfaces do not use PascalCase across cache.ts, cli.ts, config.ts, engine.ts and others.
SonarQube delta: cognitive complexity +55 with +3 smells and +1 bug introduced in a single greenfield commit, indicating unwieldy new code.
package-lock.json declares package name "ssg" and SSG dependencies, mismatching the deleted Todo API project — the dependency graph no longer reflects the seed baseline.

strengths: Added jest.config.ts/ts-jest test infrastructure, so the new code has a configured test harness rather than none.
Committed package-lock.json for dependency pinning/reproducible installs.
commit_reviews.summary: This greenfield session destroyed the Todo API seed and replaced it with an unrelated SSG project (per package-lock "ssg"/gray-matter/marked), carrying 61 convention violations, +55 cognitive complexity, and +1 bug — a net-negative architectural divergence where my qualitative judgment agrees with the mechanical measurements.

problems.description: Measured cognitive complexity +27 and duplications +13.6%: buildPageContext/site.pages plumbing plus the four near-identical test fixtures (makeTempDir/write boilerplate repeated per case) grow the module's complexity footprint.

Page now exposes template and layout as top-level fields that merely re-surface frontmatter values, which is also being added to the interface — redundant duplication of the same data through two channels.
layout?: string | false overloads a string field with a boolean sentinel for 'no layout'; a dedicated option or null is a cleaner typed contract, though false-to-disable is a recognized pattern.
Adds a new runtime dependency (handlebars ^4.7.9) for the template layer — mature and appropriate, but a new supply-chain surface for a feature that could have been a thin hand-rolled renderer.

strengths: TemplateEngine is a cohesive, option-driven abstraction with sensible defaults (templates dir, default template/layout) that slots cleanly into the existing buildSite pipeline.
Strong test coverage — 187 lines covering frontmatter-driven templates, layout wrapping via {{{body}}}, blank layout opt-out, and partials wired through site.pages for nav.
Respects existing patterns: BuildOptions-defaults convention, colocated src/*.test.ts files, and PascalCase interfaces/functions consistent with the rest of index.ts.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-tested, cleanly-abstracted template/layout engine that fits the SSG architecture and improves on the previous hardcoded renderPage, at the cost of modest added complexity and duplication plus some redundant interface fields.

problems.description: @types/ws is declared under dependencies in package.json (and lockfile), but type-only packages belong in devDependencies alongside @types/jest.

Mechanical scan reports 61 naming violations (Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase, Functions should not use snake_case) across cli.ts and other modules; the touched cli.ts itself carries new violations, driving the convention score to 0.59.

Cognitive complexity increased by +42 in a single session with +497/-29 lines; the CLI arg-dispatch/help routing (VALUE_OPTIONS map, command branches) is over-engineered for a two-command CLI and should be decomposed.

strengths: The serve command with live-reload (chokidar watcher + ws WebSocket push) is a natural, architecturally appropriate extension of the static-site-generator flow, reusing the existing buildSite() path.
Handlebars is correctly promoted from devDependencies to runtime dependencies, matching the server's runtime template rendering.
Subcommand-based CLI with per-command help text is a clean, conventional UX pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a genuinely useful live-reload dev server that fits the SSG architecture, but the commit introduces substantial naming-convention debt (0.59 score, 61 violations including in the touched cli.ts) and a +42 spike in cognitive complexity that make the net impact neutral.

problems.description: Config and plugin loading use runtime require() on .ts files; the JSDoc itself admits ssg.config.ts only loads when ts-node/tsx is active, so the primary config path silently no-ops in normal builds and the bare catch swallows the reason.

Resolution-base mismatch: loadConfig/buildPlugins resolve against process.cwd() while createEngine resolves contentDir/outputDir from BuildOptions, so a caller passing explicit options can get config/plugins from a different directory than the engine's.
Silent empty catch blocks in loadConfig and resolvePluginModule erase all diagnostics (a missing module and a crash inside a plugin both look identical); at minimum a warning is warranted.

resolvePluginModule uses duck-typing (typeof exported.name === 'string') to accept plugin instances instead of validating against the Plugin interface, making the structural contract implicit and fragile.

Measured convention score 0.59 with 61 violations (Classes/Interfaces must be PascalCase, Functions must not use snake_case) across cache.ts/cli.ts/config.ts/engine.ts; the shown diff is camelCase/PascalCase-correct, so the low score appears driven by the truncated portion of the diff — discrepancy flagged.
SonarQube delta shows cognitive complexity +38 and +3 smells despite the refactor, indicating the decomposition added orchestration indirection even while cutting duplication (-2.0%).

strengths: Clean separation of concerns: index.ts's monolith is split into config loading (config.ts) and engine orchestration (engine.ts), each with a single responsibility.
Reduces duplication by 2.0% and preserves the existing PluginPipeline/MarkdownPlugin/TemplatePlugin structure rather than inventing new machinery.
Correct recursive markdown discovery, normalized cross-platform slug derivation, and HTML-escaped titles/links (XSS-safe output).
Well-documented public entry points (buildPlugins, createEngine, buildSite) with typed interfaces.
commit_reviews.summary: A genuinely better modularization that cuts duplication and honors the existing plugin layer, but silent require()-based TS config loading, a process.cwd()/options resolution mismatch, and rising complexity leave measurable debt.

problems.description: templateHash fingerprints only template/layout/partial files; plugin code and engine version are excluded, so incremental builds can silently serve stale HTML after a markdown/plugin or engine upgrade — the only escapes are a manual CACHE_VERSION bump or --clean

buildSite() grew a deeply nested skip/reconstruct branch (SonarQube cognitive complexity +43); the incremental decision logic (hash compare + pageFromCache + manifest writeback) could be extracted from the orchestration function

Cached pages bypass pipeline.runFileSync entirely, so plugins with per-file onFile side effects no longer run for unchanged pages — a documented-but-easy-to-miss behavior change for third-party plugins
Full rendered HTML plus frontmatter is persisted inside the JSON manifest, duplicating the output directory and growing the cache file with site size

SonarQube reports convention score 0.59 with 61 violations, but the cited examples look like analyzer artifacts — config.ts is untouched by this commit and cache.ts/cli.ts interfaces (CacheEntry, CacheManifest, CliOptions) are already PascalCase; the low score appears misattributed or pre-existing

strengths: Incremental cache cleanly factored into its own module with small, pure, well-documented functions (hashContent, loadManifest, computeTemplateHash)
commit_reviews.summary: A well-architected, thoroughly-tested incremental-build feature that respects the plugin pipeline, though its cache fingerprint omits plugin/engine version (stale-output risk) and the mechanical convention score (0.59) is contradicted by the actual code style, which the diff consistently follows.

compounding_issues: Committed node_modules (~5,130 files in session 1, more in session 3) with no .gitignore ever created — repo bloat persisted across all sessions and was never remediated
dist/ build artifacts (46 files) committed to git alongside source throughout the story
Seed codebase was a Todo API (Express + sqlite), mismatched with the SSG story; session 1 discarded it entirely rather than reusing any seams, so the 'greenfield' carried zero useful prior context
No sample content/ directory shipped — `npx ssg build` produces 0 pages out of the box in the repo (only test temp dirs exercise it)
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the mismatched Todo-API seed and greenfielded the SSG in a fresh src/ layout (deleted root index.ts)
Chose Handlebars (.hbs) for the template engine with built-in default template/layout fallbacks, preserving pre-existing output when no templates directory exists

Session 4's plugin-pipeline refactor — Plugin interface, PluginPipeline, Markdown/Template/DevServer plugins, ssg.config.ts — kept the external API unchanged (verified via .d.ts), creating the seam session 5 built on
Session 5 incremental caching: SHA-256 fingerprints of source + template/layout/partials stored in .ssg-cache.json with skip-and-reconstruct-from-cache, exposed via --incremental/--clean CLI flags
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Test coverage grew monotonically (13 -> 23 -> 28 -> 28 -> 37 tests, all passing at every commit), while the architecture evolved from a 239-line monolith that did everything into cleanly separated modules (markdown, templates, config, plugin, cache, serve, engine). The pivotal session 4 refactor preserved the external API exactly — all 28 existing tests passed unchanged — which gave session 5 a clean plugin seam to bolt incremental caching onto. The final cache layer is genuinely correct: verified end-to-end that unchanged pages are skipped, template changes invalidate the fingerprint, and reconstructed HTML matches. Confidence was a flat 1.0 each session (overconfident, but the outcome supported it). The only real regression is repo hygiene: node_modules and dist artifacts were committed early and never cleaned up.
story_review.summary: A logically sequenced, consistently green five-session arc (greenfield -> templates -> dev server -> plugin refactor -> incremental caching) with disciplined API stability across the refactor and expanding test coverage — let down only by committed node_modules/dist and a discarded mismatched seed.
